source_text: Igitur ad nascentes generantium, non flagitia, sed semina pervehuntur; vim autem seminum Deus instituit, et sicut confiteri cogeris, benedixit.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore to those being born not the shameful acts of those generating, but seeds, are carried; but God instituted the force of seeds, and, as you are compelled to confess, blessed it.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS nascor; Blaise infants in the original-sin debate
LS benedico; Blaise God blessing marriage

pass_b_english: Therefore what passes from those who beget to those born is not their shameful conduct but their seed. God instituted the power of seed and, as you are compelled to confess, blessed it.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
